comment: Agent NDA identity, offer bytes and digests (agentnda.net 0.1.2-draft, 4.1, 6, 6.1, 8). Harbor & Line Outfitters signs an open offer to gate its freight-audit posting; Caldera Freight Systems accepts it. Pins the bytes where two implementations drift: the identifier hashes the version-1 offer minus id and signatures, with no prefix; the signed bytes are 'agent-nda-v1', one newline, then the JCS of the document minus signatures (id included); the offer bytes are re-derived from the completed document by setting parties.recipient and disclosure.recipient back to null; the offer digest and the agreement digest are 'sha256:' and 64 lowercase hex over those signed bytes. The agent keys in the seats are stand-ins in the family's key spelling, because the identifier and digests hash them; the language hash is the hash of a stand-in template. The signature records are real: each owner key is an Ed25519 key derived from a published test seed (nda-lifecycle.json, keys), each sig is the padded base64 of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature, and Ed25519 is deterministic, so any implementation reproduces them. Signatures are excluded from every byte string here, so they change no identifier and no digest. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: change it only with a spec change alongside.

purpose.statement: Evaluating and responding to Harbor & Line's freight-audit posting, which names this offer, and running validation probes, negotiating, and performing any Agent SoW between the parties that names this agreement.

signature.over: the signed bytes of the completed document

traps.why: the id hashes the bytes minus id AND signatures, without the prefix; hashing the signed bytes gives a different id
digests are over the signed bytes, which exclude signatures; adding a signature never changes a digest
an Agent SoW names the agreement digest (recipient filled); the offer digest is what a gated posting names
digests are lowercase hex and compared exactly
any change beyond parties.recipient and disclosure.recipient makes the re-derived offer bytes differ, and the discloser's signature fails
